section_summary: This section chiefly concerns the Japanese naval transport Asaka Maru: its voyage to Europe, proposed carriage of German goods, British contraband controls, and its changed return route. It also records Japanese warship and transport movements around East and Southeast Asia, naval intelligence reports, and later reports of Japanese submarines. Several documents appear in duplicate or as paraphrases.

people.name: Ivan Lebedeff
people.role: Caller offering a suggestion about Japanese naval policy

people.name: Coville
people.role: State Department memorandum recipient or author

people.name: K. M. Stall
people.role: Captain of the tanker W. S. Miller

people.name: Colonel Saito
people.role: Representative of the Japanese mission in southern Indochina

people.name: Y. Mito
people.role: Rear admiral, Japanese naval mission to Germany

people.name: McHugh
people.role: Source of Hong Kong station ship report

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram 416 on Asaka
subfiles.about: The Asaka sought a British port call after loading German machinery at Bilbao.
subfiles.summary: British officials offered a port call subject to contraband control; Japan had not replied.

subfiles.title: Paraphrases of Tokyo telegram 416
subfiles.about: Paraphrases relay the Asaka port-call and contraband-control report.
subfiles.summary: Two versions restate the British conditions and the transport's cargo of German stores and machinery.

subfiles.title: Legal adviser's note on public-vessel status
subfiles.about: A naval auxiliary need not lose public-vessel status merely by carrying government cargo.
subfiles.summary: Hackworth advises against discussing the legal issue with Britain.

subfiles.title: British reply on Asaka Maru, damaged copy
subfiles.about: Britain explains its blockade position and concern over Asaka Maru's cargo.
subfiles.summary: A damaged copy discusses the Nagara Maru precedent, seizure under reprisals, warship immunity, and the possible importance of Asaka Maru's cargo.

subfiles.title: British aide-mémoire on Asaka Maru
subfiles.about: Britain answers U.S. questions about blocking enemy exports aboard Asaka Maru.
subfiles.summary: Britain says the Nagara Maru concession rested on a clear understanding that enemy exports would not again be allowed through. It invokes the 1939 Reprisals Order, argues a warship carrying such goods loses immunity, and seeks more cargo intelligence from Lisbon and Bilbao.

subfiles.title: Second copy of British aide-mémoire
subfiles.about: A duplicate sets out Britain's legal and diplomatic position on Asaka Maru.
subfiles.summary: This copy repeats the Nagara Maru understanding, the British reprisal argument, and the concern that the cargo was important.

subfiles.title: Saigon telegram 37
subfiles.about: The destroyer Isokaze departed Saigon, leaving bomber crews and aircraft at the airport.
subfiles.summary: No Japanese war vessels remained in Saigon.

subfiles.title: Navy relay of Saigon telegram 37
subfiles.about: State relays Isokaze's departure and the remaining bombers.
subfiles.summary: The paraphrase was teletyped to Navy.

subfiles.title: Saigon telegram 41
subfiles.about: Isokaze returned to embark Japanese bomber ground crews and repair equipment.
subfiles.summary: A source expected the bombers to depart shortly.

subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Saigon telegram 41
subfiles.about: State circulates news of Isokaze's return to Saigon.
subfiles.summary: The report was telephoned to military intelligence and confirmed in writing.

subfiles.title: Hornbeck routing note
subfiles.about: Watt's attached letter contains three marked points of information.
subfiles.summary: A brief note introduces the Australian Legation letter.

subfiles.title: Australian Legation letter on Japan and Thailand
subfiles.about: Sir John Latham assesses Japanese moves and influence in Thailand and French Indochina.
subfiles.summary: Latham saw no confirmed bases or immediate southward move but warned that Japanese dominance of Thailand would threaten Singapore.

subfiles.title: Navy request about convoy sighting
subfiles.about: Navy seeks details of about 25 Japanese transports and escort ships seen near Kobe.
subfiles.summary: It asks officers to interview passengers arriving at Honolulu aboard President Cleveland.

subfiles.title: Japanese Embassy note on Asaka's route
subfiles.about: Asaka would not return through the Panama Canal.
subfiles.summary: The ambassador asks State to notify relevant U.S. authorities.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Japanese Ambassador
subfiles.about: State acknowledges Asaka's changed itinerary.
subfiles.summary: Interested federal authorities were informed.

subfiles.title: War Department acknowledgment
subfiles.from: Secretary of War Henry L. Stimson
subfiles.about: The Panama Canal Department was told Asaka would not transit on its return.
subfiles.summary: The second page is a copy of the acknowledgment.

subfiles.title: British aide-mémoire on Asaka Maru cargo
subfiles.about: Britain seeks U.S. views on intercepting Asaka Maru's prospective enemy-origin cargo.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum traces Asaka Maru's mission to Lisbon and lists suspected German and other European naval supplies. Britain argues the ship could be intercepted despite its naval status, but fears a major clash with Japan. It asks for an early U.S. view before loading begins.

subfiles.title: U.S. reply to British aide-mémoire, draft
subfiles.about: State questions the legal basis and practical value of intercepting Asaka Maru.
subfiles.summary: The draft seeks clarification of the Nagara Maru arrangement and blockade terminology, and cautions against raising a poorly founded issue.

subfiles.title: U.S. aide-mémoire, first copy
subfiles.about: State expresses doubts about intercepting Asaka Maru.
subfiles.summary: The U.S. questions the blockade basis, the legal support for seizure, and the cargo's naval importance.

subfiles.title: U.S. aide-mémoire, second copy
subfiles.about: A further copy records U.S. legal concerns over an Asaka Maru interception.
subfiles.summary: State says it would avoid raising an issue unless its position was well founded.

subfiles.title: Second copy of British aide-mémoire
subfiles.about: Britain requests consultation before subjecting Asaka Maru to contraband control.
subfiles.summary: This copy repeats the suspected cargo, British interception argument, risk of provoking Japan, and request for prompt U.S. views.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: military policy toward Japan
subfiles.about: Points to a memorandum on Ivan Lebedeff's suggestion of a surprise attack on Japan's navy.
subfiles.summary: References file 711.94/2045.

subfiles.title: Saigon telegram 43
subfiles.about: Isokaze and the Japanese bombers left Saigon.
subfiles.summary: Flood believed only Colonel Saito and possible civilian assistants remained in Cochinchina.

subfiles.title: Routing note on naval transport Asaka
subfiles.about: Calls attention to a naval attaché report on Asaka's possible machinery cargo.
subfiles.summary: The note refers to attached intelligence reports.

subfiles.title: Naval attaché report 24-41: Asaka to Europe
subfiles.from: H. H. Smith-Hutton, Naval Attaché, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Asaka's European voyage, German machinery shipment, and Panama Canal guard dispute.
subfiles.summary: The report describes the ship's schedule, armament, and suspected mission to carry German machinery to Japan. It reproduces Japan's objection to armed U.S. guards during the canal transit and records the U.S. refusal to exempt the vessel.

subfiles.title: Naval attaché report 21-41: mission to Germany
subfiles.from: H. H. Smith-Hutton, Naval Attaché, Tokyo
subfiles.about: A Japanese naval technical mission sailed aboard Asaka for Germany.
subfiles.summary: The report lists naval officers and civilian personnel, suggests they would study German naval and aircraft equipment and production, and gives Lisbon as the expected arrival port.

subfiles.title: Hong Kong report on possible troop transports
subfiles.from: John H. Bruins, American Consul, Hong Kong
subfiles.about: A tanker captain saw four large darkened ships heading toward Hainan.
subfiles.summary: Captain Stall could not identify the ships but thought they might be Japanese troop transports. Bruins informed the senior British naval officer.

subfiles.title: State Department note on Akagi Maru
subfiles.about: Flags a report suggesting Akagi Maru could supply raiders at sea.
subfiles.summary: It highlights stevedoring gear and blackout equipment.

subfiles.title: War Department transmission
subfiles.about: Forwards the Akagi Maru search report.
subfiles.summary: The letter transmits an intelligence enclosure for possible action.

subfiles.title: Search report extract on Akagi Maru
subfiles.about: Customs officers found unusual cargo-handling and blackout equipment aboard Akagi Maru.
subfiles.summary: The equipment raised suspicion of supplying raiders, although the search found no contraband.

subfiles.title: Coast Guard report on Asaka
subfiles.about: Asaka left Lisbon on February 23, apparently bound for Japan.
subfiles.summary: The message reports the vessel's departure.

subfiles.title: Shanghai naval attaché report
subfiles.about: Reports Eritrea at Kobe and a large Japanese fleet near Ariake Bay.
subfiles.summary: The report also notes passenger-transport restrictions to Nagasaki.

subfiles.title: State notice to War Department on Asaka
subfiles.about: Asaka would not return through the Panama Canal.
subfiles.summary: Three copies relay the ambassador's notice.

subfiles.title: Tokyo naval attaché fleet report
subfiles.about: About 40 ships of Japan's Combined Fleet were reported in a bay near Toyohashi.
subfiles.summary: The short report locates a major concentration of ships.

subfiles.title: Shanghai report on possible troop movements
subfiles.about: A source described possible use of Asama Maru and Kamakura Maru as troop transports.
subfiles.summary: The report also notes infantry arrivals from Osaka, movement toward Taiwan, and purchases of Burma maps.

subfiles.title: Hong Kong station ship transport report
subfiles.about: British observers reported Japanese transports and landing craft in the Pearl River.
subfiles.summary: A later reconnaissance found most vessels gone and no evidence of troop loading.

subfiles.title: Manila radiogram on Japanese carriers and aircraft
subfiles.about: British sources reported carriers, aircraft, and southward Japanese shipping in the western Pacific.
subfiles.summary: The report names Kaga and enumerates aircraft at Wotje, Jaluit, Truk, Saipan, and Palau.

subfiles.title: Navy memorandum on Japanese battleships
subfiles.about: A Thai attaché reported new Japanese battleships and planned pocket battleships.
subfiles.summary: The report gives estimated tonnage, guns, and commissioning dates.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: Japanese merchant vessels
subfiles.about: Points to a confidential telegram on Japanese merchant-vessel movements.
subfiles.summary: References file 894.8591/786.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: submarines off Red Sea
subfiles.about: Points to a telegram on possible Japanese submarines near the Red Sea entrance.
subfiles.summary: References file 740.0011.P.W./992.

subfiles.title: Hoover letter on submarines off Peru
subfiles.about: A source reported two Japanese submarines provisioned off Chicama, Peru.
subfiles.summary: Hoover says the intelligence had already been telephoned to State and Naval Intelligence.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference: Spanish bunkers for Axis submarines
subfiles.about: Points to a telegram on accusations involving Spanish merchant vessels and Axis submarines.
subfiles.summary: References file 852.801/27.

subfiles.title: Bern telegram on Japanese submarine at Bordeaux
subfiles.about: A Japanese submarine reportedly landed about 20 diplomats at Bordeaux.
subfiles.summary: The report suggests Japan maintained long-distance submarine links with European allies.
